Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 57, verses 1–8:

Medinan. It has 2,476 letters, 544 words and 29 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Muqri informed us: Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili related to us, and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani related to us, both saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbu'i related to us: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini related to us: Harun ibn Kathir related to us: Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Hadid will be written among those who believed in Allah and His Messenger." [214] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/381.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Competent. He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾

"He is the First" means: prior to every thing, without limit or beginning; He was, and nothing else existed. "And the Last" means: after the annihilation of every thing. "And the Manifest" means: the Dominant, the Exalted over every thing, and everything is beneath Him. "And the Hidden" means: the One who knows every thing, so no one knows more than Him.

This is the meaning reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn 'Umar said: "The First" by creating, "the Last" by providing sustenance, "the Manifest" by giving life, and "the Hidden" by causing death.

al-Dahhak said: He is the One who is the first of the first and the last of the last, the most manifest of the manifest and the most hidden of the hidden.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He is the First without anyone's interpretation, the Last without anyone's delay, the Manifest without anyone's making manifest, and the Hidden without anyone's concealing.

Yaman said: He is the First, the Eternal; the Last, the Merciful; the Manifest, the Forbearing; and the Hidden, the All-Knowing.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said: The First by His kindness, the Last by His pardon, the Manifest by His beneficence, and the Hidden by His secrecy.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He is the First by pre-eternity, the Last by everlastingness, the Manifest by oneness, and the Hidden by self-sufficiency.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: These waws are superfluous and the meaning is: He is the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, because whoever is first among us cannot be last, and whoever is manifest cannot be hidden.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is the First without beginning, the Last without end, the Manifest without approach, and the Hidden without veiling.

al-Qannad said: "The First" is the one who precedes in doing good and who goes before every benefactor in performing benevolence; "the Last" is the one who remains after the disappearance of creation, and the Seal through the performance of beneficence; "the Manifest" is the one who prevails over everyone, for whoever prevails over something has overcome it. "The Manifest" also means the one who knows outward things and is aware of inner secrets. "The Manifest" also means: He is apparent to minds through information, and apparent to spirits through certainty, even if He is hidden from the eyes of observers. "The Hidden" is the one who knows the unseen and is aware of what is concealed. "The Hidden" also means: the one who is hidden from outward things, so He is not perceived except through inner secrets.

al-Suddi said: "The First" by His kindness, in that He made you know His oneness; "the Last" by His generosity, in that He made you know repentance for what you committed; "the Manifest" by His guidance, in that He enabled you to prostrate to Him; and "the Hidden" by His concealment, in that when you disobeyed Him He covered it over for you.

Ibn 'Ata' said: "The First" by disclosing the conditions of this world so that they do not desire it; "the Last" by disclosing the conditions of the Hereafter so that they do not doubt it; "the Manifest" upon the hearts of His friends so that they know Him; and "the Hidden" from the hearts of His enemies so that they deny Him.

It was said: "The First" before every known thing; "the Last" after every sealed thing; "the Manifest" above every drawn thing; and "the Hidden" encompassing every concealed thing.

It was said: He is the First by the all-encompassing knowledge of our sins before our sins existed; the Last by covering them over us in our final state; the Manifest by preserving us in our worldly life; and the Hidden by purifying our secrets and cleansing our remembrances.

It was said: He is the First by creation, its explanation being His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [[Surat Ya-Sin: 82.]]; and the Last by guidance, its explanation being His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe﴾ [[Surat Ibrahim: 27.]] etc.

And the Manifest by clarification, its explanation being His saying: ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 26.]]; and the Hidden by adornment, its explanation being His saying: ﴿and He has made it beloved in your hearts﴾ [[Surat al-Hujurat: 7.]].

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: The First by composition, the Last by obligation, the Manifest by disposition, and the Hidden by making known.

al-Junayd said: He is the First by expanding hearts, the Last by forgiving sins, the Manifest by removing distresses, and the Hidden by knowledge of the unseen.

'Umar asked Ka'b about this verse, and he said: Its meaning is that His knowledge of the First is like His knowledge of the Last, and His knowledge of the Manifest is like His knowledge of the Hidden.

It was said: He is the First by awe and authority, the Last by mercy and beneficence, the Manifest by proof and evidence, and the Hidden by protection and bounty.

It was said: He is the First by giving, the Last by recompense, the Manifest by praise, and the Hidden by fulfilment.

It was said: He is the First by piety and generosity, the Last by the gift of the share, the Manifest by the abundance of blessings, and the Hidden by the warding off of afflictions.

It was said: He is the First by guidance, the Last by sufficiency, the Manifest by authority, and the Hidden by care.

It was said: He is the First by bestowal, the Last by completion, the Manifest by honour, and the Hidden by inspiration.

It was said: He is the First by naming the names, the Last by perfecting blessings, the Manifest by shaping the limbs, and the Hidden by turning desires away.

It was said: He is the First by bringing creatures into being, the Last by annihilating creatures, the Manifest by manifesting realities, and the Hidden by knowledge of subtleties.

al-Wasiti said: He left no self for creatures after He informed about His own self that He is the First, the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard al-Shibli say: In this verse there are things that have fallen away, for I am first, last, manifest, hidden.

﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, a cloud came over them, and he said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "This is the 'anan, this is the water-carriers of the earth, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, drives to a people who do not thank Him nor call upon Him." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "It is the Raqi', a surging wave and a protected ceiling."

He said: "How far do you think is between you and it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Between you and it is a distance of five hundred years." He said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Above it is another heaven, between them a distance of five hundred years," until he enumerated seven heavens, between each two heavens a distance of five hundred years.

Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Above that is the Throne, and between it and the seventh heaven is a distance like that between two heavens."

Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "It is the earth."

He said: "Do you know what is beneath it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Beneath it is another earth, and between them is a distance of five hundred years," until he enumerated seven earths, between each earth a distance of five hundred years. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, if you were to lower one of you with a rope to the lowest seventh earth, he would descend upon Allah." [215] Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾, and its meaning is with knowledge, power, creation and dominion.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Abu Makki informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi informed us: Ali ibn al-Hasan related to us: Abu Hamza related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), came to him and asked him for a servant. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than that? Say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of every thing, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every thing You hold by its forelock. You are the First, there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, there is nothing after You; and You are the Manifest, there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us and enrich us from poverty.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/370; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/85; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 28/196.]] [216]

﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: Abdullah ibn al-Fadl related to me: Ahmad ibn Warkan related to us: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us, who said: I said to Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak: "How do we know our Lord, Mighty and Majestic?" He said: "In the seventh heaven, upon His Throne. And do not say, as the Jahmiyya say: 'Here, on the earth.'"

We have already mentioned the meaning of istiwa' and examined the discussion of it, so there is no need to repeat it.

﴿He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ "And He is with you" in knowledge and power. ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that of which He has made you successors (mustakhlafin) therein.﴾ "Made you successors": given dominion, and granted long life in it. ﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward.﴾ ﴿And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are believers?﴾ Mujahid said: The covenant was taken from the loins of Adam, that Allah is your Lord and there is no god for you besides Him.

It was said: "He took your covenant" by placing reason in you and establishing the proofs and evidences that call to following the Messenger.

The reading of the majority is with a fatha on the hamza and the qaf (ukhidha). Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on both, in the passive form (ukhidha, the agent unnamed). ﴿if you are believers﴾: that is, at some point in time; so now is the most fitting time for you to believe, since the proofs and signs establishing the reality of Islam and the truth of the prophethood of the Chosen One (peace be upon him) are in place.

Medinan. It has 2,476 letters, 544 words and 29 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Muqri informed us: Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili related to us, and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani related to us, both saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbu'i related to us: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini related to us: Harun ibn Kathir related to us: Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Hadid will be written among those who believed in Allah and His Messenger." [214] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/381.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Competent. He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾

"He is the First" means: prior to every thing, without limit or beginning; He was, and nothing else existed. "And the Last" means: after the annihilation of every thing. "And the Manifest" means: the Dominant, the Exalted over every thing, and everything is beneath Him. "And the Hidden" means: the One who knows every thing, so no one knows more than Him.

This is the meaning reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn 'Umar said: "The First" by creating, "the Last" by providing sustenance, "the Manifest" by giving life, and "the Hidden" by causing death.

al-Dahhak said: He is the One who is the first of the first and the last of the last, the most manifest of the manifest and the most hidden of the hidden.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He is the First without anyone's interpretation, the Last without anyone's delay, the Manifest without anyone's making manifest, and the Hidden without anyone's concealing.

Yaman said: He is the First, the Eternal; the Last, the Merciful; the Manifest, the Forbearing; and the Hidden, the All-Knowing.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said: The First by His kindness, the Last by His pardon, the Manifest by His beneficence, and the Hidden by His secrecy.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He is the First by pre-eternity, the Last by everlastingness, the Manifest by oneness, and the Hidden by self-sufficiency.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: These waws are superfluous and the meaning is: He is the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, because whoever is first among us cannot be last, and whoever is manifest cannot be hidden.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is the First without beginning, the Last without end, the Manifest without approach, and the Hidden without veiling.

al-Qannad said: "The First" is the one who precedes in doing good and who goes before every benefactor in performing benevolence; "the Last" is the one who remains after the disappearance of creation, and the Seal through the performance of beneficence; "the Manifest" is the one who prevails over everyone, for whoever prevails over something has overcome it. "The Manifest" also means the one who knows outward things and is aware of inner secrets. "The Manifest" also means: He is apparent to minds through information, and apparent to spirits through certainty, even if He is hidden from the eyes of observers. "The Hidden" is the one who knows the unseen and is aware of what is concealed. "The Hidden" also means: the one who is hidden from outward things, so He is not perceived except through inner secrets.

al-Suddi said: "The First" by His kindness, in that He made you know His oneness; "the Last" by His generosity, in that He made you know repentance for what you committed; "the Manifest" by His guidance, in that He enabled you to prostrate to Him; and "the Hidden" by His concealment, in that when you disobeyed Him He covered it over for you.

Ibn 'Ata' said: "The First" by disclosing the conditions of this world so that they do not desire it; "the Last" by disclosing the conditions of the Hereafter so that they do not doubt it; "the Manifest" upon the hearts of His friends so that they know Him; and "the Hidden" from the hearts of His enemies so that they deny Him.

It was said: "The First" before every known thing; "the Last" after every sealed thing; "the Manifest" above every drawn thing; and "the Hidden" encompassing every concealed thing.

It was said: He is the First by the all-encompassing knowledge of our sins before our sins existed; the Last by covering them over us in our final state; the Manifest by preserving us in our worldly life; and the Hidden by purifying our secrets and cleansing our remembrances.

It was said: He is the First by creation, its explanation being His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [[Surat Ya-Sin: 82.]]; and the Last by guidance, its explanation being His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe﴾ [[Surat Ibrahim: 27.]] etc.

And the Manifest by clarification, its explanation being His saying: ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 26.]]; and the Hidden by adornment, its explanation being His saying: ﴿and He has made it beloved in your hearts﴾ [[Surat al-Hujurat: 7.]].

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: The First by composition, the Last by obligation, the Manifest by disposition, and the Hidden by making known.

al-Junayd said: He is the First by expanding hearts, the Last by forgiving sins, the Manifest by removing distresses, and the Hidden by knowledge of the unseen.

'Umar asked Ka'b about this verse, and he said: Its meaning is that His knowledge of the First is like His knowledge of the Last, and His knowledge of the Manifest is like His knowledge of the Hidden.

It was said: He is the First by awe and authority, the Last by mercy and beneficence, the Manifest by proof and evidence, and the Hidden by protection and bounty.

It was said: He is the First by giving, the Last by recompense, the Manifest by praise, and the Hidden by fulfilment.

It was said: He is the First by piety and generosity, the Last by the gift of the share, the Manifest by the abundance of blessings, and the Hidden by the warding off of afflictions.

It was said: He is the First by guidance, the Last by sufficiency, the Manifest by authority, and the Hidden by care.

It was said: He is the First by bestowal, the Last by completion, the Manifest by honour, and the Hidden by inspiration.

It was said: He is the First by naming the names, the Last by perfecting blessings, the Manifest by shaping the limbs, and the Hidden by turning desires away.

It was said: He is the First by bringing creatures into being, the Last by annihilating creatures, the Manifest by manifesting realities, and the Hidden by knowledge of subtleties.

al-Wasiti said: He left no self for creatures after He informed about His own self that He is the First, the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Razi say: I heard al-Shibli say: In this verse there are things that have fallen away, for I am first, last, manifest, hidden.

﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, a cloud came over them, and he said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "This is the 'anan, this is the water-carriers of the earth, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, drives to a people who do not thank Him nor call upon Him." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "It is the Raqi', a surging wave and a protected ceiling."

He said: "How far do you think is between you and it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Between you and it is a distance of five hundred years." He said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Above it is another heaven, between them a distance of five hundred years," until he enumerated seven heavens, between each two heavens a distance of five hundred years.

Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Above that is the Throne, and between it and the seventh heaven is a distance like that between two heavens."

Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "It is the earth."

He said: "Do you know what is beneath it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Beneath it is another earth, and between them is a distance of five hundred years," until he enumerated seven earths, between each earth a distance of five hundred years. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, if you were to lower one of you with a rope to the lowest seventh earth, he would descend upon Allah." [215] Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾, and its meaning is with knowledge, power, creation and dominion.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Abu Makki informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi informed us: Ali ibn al-Hasan related to us: Abu Hamza related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), came to him and asked him for a servant. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than that? Say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of every thing, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every thing You hold by its forelock. You are the First, there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, there is nothing after You; and You are the Manifest, there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us and enrich us from poverty.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/370; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/85; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 28/196.]] [216]

﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us: Abdullah ibn al-Fadl related to me: Ahmad ibn Warkan related to us: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us, who said: I said to Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak: "How do we know our Lord, Mighty and Majestic?" He said: "In the seventh heaven, upon His Throne. And do not say, as the Jahmiyya say: 'Here, on the earth.'"

We have already mentioned the meaning of istiwa' and examined the discussion of it, so there is no need to repeat it.

﴿He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ "And He is with you" in knowledge and power. ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that of which He has made you successors (mustakhlafin) therein.﴾ "Made you successors": given dominion, and granted long life in it. ﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward.﴾ ﴿And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are believers?﴾ Mujahid said: The covenant was taken from the loins of Adam, that Allah is your Lord and there is no god for you besides Him.

It was said: "He took your covenant" by placing reason in you and establishing the proofs and evidences that call to following the Messenger.

The reading of the majority is with a fatha on the hamza and the qaf (ukhidha). Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on both, in the passive form (ukhidha, the agent unnamed). ﴿if you are believers﴾: that is, at some point in time; so now is the most fitting time for you to believe, since the proofs and signs establishing the reality of Islam and the truth of the prophethood of the Chosen One (peace be upon him) are in place.

He is the One who sends down to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) clear signs, so that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. ﴿Indeed, Allah is toward you Compassionate and Merciful.﴾

It was also said:

It is the Messenger who brings you out, through the call (al-da'wa), from the darknesses into the light. ﴿And indeed, Allah is toward you Compassionate and Merciful.﴾

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth?﴾ Then He (glory be to Him) explained the excellence of those who were foremost in spending and in jihad, so He, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest.﴾ That is, the conquest (fath) of Makkah, according to the saying of most exegetes (mufassirun).

Al-Sha'bi said: It is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya. He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of Allah, was it a conquest?" He said: "Yes, a great one." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/287.]

﴿And fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).﴾

﴿They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward﴾, that is, after the conquest.

Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn al-Barqi related to me, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abu Sa'id al-Tammar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will soon come a people whose deeds you will consider insignificant compared with their deeds."

It was asked: Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? "Quraysh?"

He said: "No, they are more tender of heart and softer of hearts." He pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said: "They are the people of Yemen. Indeed, faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they better than us?"

He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them had a mountain of gold and spent it, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor even half of it." Then he gathered his fingers and extended his little finger and said: "Indeed, this is the excellence that lies between us and the people: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought.﴾" [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/288.] [217]

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from al-Kalbi that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). In this verse there is a clear indication and a manifest proof of the excellence of Abu Bakr through his precedence, because he was the first to embrace Islam.

[Footnote: The narration from the Prophet, the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un) agrees that Ali was the first to embrace Islam, the first to pray, and the first to believe.

(The reality of Ali's (peace be upon him) Islam) It is established that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was the first to follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with awareness and certainty.

Al-Mas'udi said, concerning one who belittled the Commander because of his young age at the time of his Islam: This is the statement of one who intended to remove his virtues and repel his merits, so as to make his Islam the Islam of a small child, a youth without discernment, who cannot distinguish excellence from deficiency, nor tell doubt from certainty, nor recognize truth to seek it or falsehood to avoid it. (al-Tanbih wa'l-Ashraf: 198, chapter on the history from the birth of the Messenger.)

He said: Many people went to the view that he had never associated anything with Allah, and so he did not need to renew Islam. (Muruj al-Dhahab: 2/400, Cairo ed. 1346 AH; Beirut ed. 2/276, chapter on his mission and what came of it until his migration.)

Al-Maqrizi said: As for Ali, he never associated partners with Allah at all. When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he informed Khadija, and she affirmed it, he and Ali were together. Ali did not need to be called, nor was he a polytheist who would then need to be made a monotheist so that it could be said he "embraced Islam." This is the verified position. (Imta' al-Asma': 1/16-17, edited by Mahmud Shakir, Cairo ed.)

Something similar is related from al-Amiri. (al-Riyad al-Mustabata: 168, his biography.)

Abu Ja'far al-Iskafi said, after mentioning the hadith of the house: Would a child who is not discerning and not sensible be charged with preparing the food and calling the people? Would a child be entrusted with the secret of prophethood? Would anyone be counted among the elders and the grown men except an intelligent and judicious person? Would the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) place his hand in his, and give him the handshake of allegiance, with the promise of the brotherhood, the bequest and the caliphate, unless he were fit for that? He who had reached the limit of responsibility, who could bear the guardianship of Allah and the enmity of His enemies. What is it with this child who did not become attached to his peers, did not join those of his kind, and was not seen among the boys in their games after his Islam?

Rather, we have seen him only persisting in his Islam, resolute in his affair, making his word true by his deed. He confirmed his Islam through his chastity and asceticism, and he clung to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more than anyone present.

He (peace be upon him) also mentioned in his speeches and sermons the beginning of his condition and the opening of his affair, when he embraced Islam when the Messenger of Allah called the tree, and it came toward him dragging along the earth. Quraysh said: "A sorcerer, a great sorcerer."

Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am the first to believe in you. I believed in Allah and His Messenger, and I affirmed you in what you brought. I bear witness that the tree did what it did by the command of Allah, as confirmation of your prophethood and as proof of your call."

Could there ever be a faith more sound than this faith? More firm in its bond and more steadfast in its strength? But the bias of the Uthmaniyya, their rage, the partisanship of al-Jahiz and his deviation are things with no remedy. (Sharh al-Nahj: 13/244, sermon 238; and al-Ghadir: 2/287, citing his book 'Ala al-Uthmaniyya.)

(Ali was the first to embrace Islam) Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said in al-Isti'ab: It is related from Salman, Abu Dhar, al-Miqdad, Khabbab, Jabir, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Zayd ibn Arqam that "Ali ibn Abi Talib was the first to embrace Islam," and these preferred him over others. (al-Isti'ab: 3/15, biography of Ali; and Jawahir al-'Iqdayn: 462, chapter fifteen.)

The hadith of his being the first to embrace Islam has been related from each of: Zayd ibn Arqam (Musnad Ahmad: 4/367-371, ed. M; and 5/499, ed. B; and Sahih al-Tirmidhi: 5/642, nos. 3734-3735). And from Habba al-'Urani (Musnad Abi Hanifa: 247, Cairo ed.), Jabir (al-Isaba: 8/183, part 1, Cairo ed.), al-Harith (Usd al-Ghaba: 5/520), Ibn 'Abbas (Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/133; and Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 45, no. 23), Abu Hurayra (Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/605, no. 32925), Malik ibn al-Huwayrith (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 19/291, his biography), Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/465, virtues of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari), 'Affif al-Kindi (Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/183, virtues of Khadija), Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/500, virtues of Sa'd), 'Umar (Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 58; and Sharh al-Nahj of Ibn Abi'l-Hadid: 13/230, sermon 238), Salman, al-Miqdad, Abu Sa'id, Khabbab and Abu Dhar (Sharh al-Nahj of Ibn Abi'l-Hadid: 13/230, sermon 238; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 5/84, no. 4652, biography of Zayd ibn al-Harith, and 6/265, biography of Salman, what was related from him by al-Kindi; al-Isti'ab: 2/458; and Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/136, virtues of the Amir), Abu Rafi' and Buraida (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/452, biography of Khadija; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/220, Cairo ed.; Bughyat al-Ra'id fi Tahqiq Majma' al-Zawa'id: 353, no. 15258; and al-Awa'il: 30, no. 70), Anas (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/411, biography of Fatima), Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (Muruj al-Dhahab: 2/59, Cairo ed. 1346 AH; and Beirut ed. 3/11, chapter on Mu'awiya), al-Hasan (peace be upon him) (al-Isti'ab: 2/458; and al-Hilya: 4/294, Cairo ed. 1351), al-Kalbi (Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/57, chapter on the first to embrace Islam), Ibn 'Awf (al-Futuh of Ibn A'tham: 1/217, Ali's letter to Mu'awiya), 'Urwa and Salman ibn Yasar (A'lam al-Nubuwwa: 205, chapter 12), al-Miqdad, Habban, Jabir and al-Hasan al-Basri (al-A'imma al-Ithna 'Ashar: 48), al-A'mash (Manaqib of Ibn al-Maghazili: 107, Beirut ed.; and Tehran ed.: 151, no. 188), Abu Ayyub and Umm Salama (Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 353, no. 364, chapter 20; and 112, chapter 9, no. 122), al-Sadiq from his fathers (Sharh al-Nahj of Ibn Abi'l-Hadid: 13/227, sermon 238), and 'A'isha and Asma' (Fath al-Malik al-'Ali: 67).

(Ali was the first to pray) The hadith has been related from each of: Ibn 'Abbas (Minhat al-Ma'bud: 1/89-180, nos. 2323-2657; and al-Kamil fi'l-Tarikh: 1/484, mention of disagreement about who first embraced Islam), Habba al-'Urani (al-Awa'il: 30, no. 68; al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 3/15, biography of Ali; and Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 19, no. 1), Zayd ibn Arqam and Abu Hamza (Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 22 and 26, nos. 2 and 4; Usd al-Ghaba: 4/17; Musnad Ahmad: 1/141, and 4/370, ed. M; and 1/227, and 5/498, ed. B), Mujahid (al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 3/13, part 1, Leiden ed. 1322; and 3/15, biography of Ali, Beirut ed., Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyya), Ibn Ishaq and Jabir (Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/55, Cairo ed. 1357; Sharh al-Nahj: 13/229, sermon 238; and Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/281, Beirut ed., and 1/262, Halabi ed., Cairo), Abu Mas'ud (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 10/184, biography of Ibn Mas'ud, no. 10397), Anas ibn Malik (Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 59; Sharh al-Nahj: 13/228, sermon 238; and Sahih al-Tirmidhi: 5/642, no. 3734), Buraida (Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/112, mention of his Islam from the Kitab al-Ma'rifa), 'Affif al-Kindi (Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 27, no. 5; Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/183, virtues of Khadija; and al-Kamil fi'l-Tarikh: 1/484), Ibn Mas'ud (Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/56), al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna (Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 59), Rafi' (Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 59; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 57, no. 24), 'Abd Allah ibn Nujayy (Tarjamat 'Ali: 1/64, nos. 91 and 92), 'Amr ibn al-'As (al-Futuh: 1/401, Siffin), and Hashim ibn 'Utba (al-Kamil fi'l-Tarikh: 2/384, events of the year 37).

And from Abu Ayyub, Anas, 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah and Abu Dhar (Sharh al-Nahj: 13/230, sermon 238; Tarjamat 'Ali from Tarikh Dimashq: 1/80, nos. 112 and 113; Manaqib of Ibn al-Maghazili: 25, Beirut ed., and 14, Tehran ed., nos. 17 and 19; and Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/56).

(Ali was the first to worship Allah the Exalted) It is related from Habba al-'Urani that he heard Ali say: "O Allah, I do not acknowledge that any servant of Yours from this Ummah worshipped You before me, other than your Prophet" — three times. (Musnad Ahmad: 1/99, ed. M; and 1/160, ed. B; Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 60, chapter on his being the first to pray; Muntakhab Kanz al-'Ummal: 5/40; Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/365, Cairo ed.; and 13/126, no. 36400, Beirut ed.; Usd al-Ghaba: 4/17, with variation; Kanz al-Fawa'id: 122; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/102, Cairo ed.; Bughyat al-Ra'id: 125, no. 14601; al-Isti'ab: 2/458; al-Qawl al-Musaddad: 83, tenth hadith; Zad al-Muslim fima Ittafaqa 'alayhi al-Bukhari wa-Muslim: 4/36; Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 3, Cairo ed., and 31, no. 7, Beirut ed.).

Al-Tabarani recorded it in al-Awsat with the wording: "O Allah, You know that no one from this Ummah worshipped You after its Prophet (ﷺ) before me, and I worshipped You six years before anyone from this Ummah worshipped You." (al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 2/444, no. 1767.)

(Ali was the first to believe) It is related from Mu'adha al-'Adawiyya that Ali (peace be upon him) said: "I am al-Siddiq al-Akbar. I believed in Allah before Abu Bakr believed." (Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/164, no. 36497; Tarjamat 'Ali from Tarikh Dimashq: 1/62, no. 88; Ansab al-Ashraf: 2/146, biography of Ali; and Sharh al-Nahj: 13/228, sermon 238.)

The narration of his being the first to believe has been related by each of: Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/95, no. 163, biography of Ali, Sunni; and Sharh al-Nahj: 6/288, sermon 83), 'Amr ibn 'Abbad (Khasa'is al-Nasa'i: 3, Cairo ed., "al-Taqaddum"), Layla al-Ghifariyya (al-Isti'ab: 2/759, her biography), Abu Dhar, Mu'adha al-'Adawiyya and Mu'adh ibn Jabal (al-Riyad al-Nadira: 2/157 and 198; and Ansab al-Ashraf: 2/362), Salman and Ubayy (Fayd al-Qadir: 4/258, Cairo ed. 1356; Muntakhab al-Kanz: 5/33; and Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba: 58), Abu Rafi' (Sharh al-Nahj: 13/228, sermon 238), Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (Muruj al-Dhahab: 2/59, Cairo ed. 1346 AH; and Beirut ed. 3/11, chapter on Mu'awiya), Hudhayfa (Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/616, no. 32990), Abu Sa'id and Mu'adh ibn Jabal (Hilyat al-Awliya': 1/66), 'Umar (Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/393, Cairo ed., and 13/117, no. 36378, Beirut ed.; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 55, no. 19, chapter 4), Jabir (Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 111, chapter 9, no. 120), Mu'awiya ibn Yazid (Tarikh al-Ya'qubi: 2/254, the days of Mu'awiya ibn Yazid), Ibn 'Abbas (Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/123, no. 36392), al-Miqdad (Tarikh al-Ya'qubi: 2/163, the days of 'Uthman), al-Ashtar (al-Futuh: 1/388, the battle of Siffin, what happened between Ali and Mu'awiya by letters), Ibn Shihab (Sharh al-Nahj: 1/226, sermon 6), and 'Amr ibn al-'As (al-Futuh: 1/401, mention of the people whom Mu'awiya sent to Ali).]

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid, Abu Bakr informed us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub informed us, Abu'l-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, 'Ikrima ibn 'Imad related to us, Shaddad ibn Abd Allah Abu 'Ammar related to us, and he had met a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: Abu Umama said to 'Amr ibn 'Abasa: "By what do you claim to be the fourth of Islam?" He said: "I used to see the people upon error, and I did not regard idols as anything. Then I heard of a man who was informing us of news of Makkah, so I mounted my riding camel until I came to him. His people were around him, and he said:

I said: "What are you?"

He said: "I am a prophet." I said: "And what is a prophet?" He said: "A messenger of Allah."

I said: "With what has He sent you?" He said: "That you single out Allah and not associate anything with Him, break the idols, and maintain the ties of kinship."

I said: "Who is with you in this?" He said: "A free man and a slave." And with him were Abu Bakr and Bilal. So I embraced Islam at that moment, and I saw myself as the fourth of Islam." [Sahih Muslim: 2/208.]

And because he was the first to openly manifest Islam:

Abu Muhammad al-Isfahani informed us, Abu Bakr al-Sa'i informed us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal informed us, my father informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Za'ida related to us, from Asim ibn Abi'l-Najud, from Zirr, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The first to openly manifest Islam were the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, Ammar and his mother Sumayya, Suhayb, Bilal and al-Miqdad."

And because he was the first to fight for Islam:

Abu Nasr al-Nu'man ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani informed us there, Abu'l-Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Muhammadabadi informed us, and Abu Qilaba related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Za'ida related to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The first to openly manifest Islam with his sword was the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him)."

And because he was the first to spend on the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the cause of Allah:

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayyub informed us, Muhammad ibn Yunus informed us, al-'Ala ibn 'Amr al-Shaybani related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id related to us, from Adam ibn Ali, from Ibn Umar, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and with him was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, wearing a cloak which he had fastened over his chest with a skewer. The Prophet said: 'He spent his wealth on me before the conquest.'"

He said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Read to him the greeting of peace, and say to him: Are you pleased with me in this your poverty, or are you displeased?﴾"

Abu Bakr said: "Should I be displeased? I am pleased with my Lord. I am pleased with my Lord. I am pleased with my Lord."

And for this reason the Companions preferred him over themselves and acknowledged his precedence and his priority.

And Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq informed us, Muhammad ibn Yunus, Uqba ibn Sinan, informed us, Abu Bishr related to us, al-Haythan ibn Shaddakh related to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abd Allah ibn Salama, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead, Abu Bakr prayed, and Umar a third. So whoever is brought to me preferring me over Abu Bakr and Umar, I will flog him the flogging of the slanderer, and I will dismiss his testimony!" [The memorizers of hadith weakened this hadith, because some Companions held the view that Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was preferable to the caliphs who preceded him (may Allah be pleased with them), as Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned in al-Isti'ab in the biography of Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him).]

﴿And to each Allah has promised the best, and Allah is Aware of what you do. Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He will multiply it for him, and for him there is a noble reward.﴾

He is the One who sends down to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) clear signs, so that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. ﴿Indeed, Allah is toward you Compassionate and Merciful.﴾

It was also said:

It is the Messenger who brings you out, through the call (al-da'wa), from the darknesses into the light. ﴿And indeed, Allah is toward you Compassionate and Merciful.﴾

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth?﴾ Then He (glory be to Him) explained the excellence of those who were foremost in spending and in jihad, so He, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest.﴾ That is, the conquest (fath) of Makkah, according to the saying of most exegetes (mufassirun).

Al-Sha'bi said: It is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya. He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of Allah, was it a conquest?" He said: "Yes, a great one." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/287.]

﴿And fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).﴾

﴿They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward﴾, that is, after the conquest.

Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn al-Barqi related to me, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abu Sa'id al-Tammar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will soon come a people whose deeds you will consider insignificant compared with their deeds."

It was asked: Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? "Quraysh?"

He said: "No, they are more tender of heart and softer of hearts." He pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said: "They are the people of Yemen. Indeed, faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they better than us?"

He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them had a mountain of gold and spent it, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor even half of it." Then he gathered his fingers and extended his little finger and said: "Indeed, this is the excellence that lies between us and the people: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought.﴾" [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/288.] [217]

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from al-Kalbi that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). In this verse there is a clear indication and a manifest proof of the excellence of Abu Bakr through his precedence, because he was the first to embrace Islam.

[Footnote: The narration from the Prophet, the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un) agrees that Ali was the first to embrace Islam, the first to pray, and the first to believe.

(The reality of Ali's (peace be upon him) Islam) It is established that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was the first to follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with awareness and certainty.

Al-Mas'udi said, concerning one who belittled the Commander because of his young age at the time of his Islam: This is the statement of one who intended to remove his virtues and repel his merits, so as to make his Islam the Islam of a small child, a youth without discernment, who cannot distinguish excellence from deficiency, nor tell doubt from certainty, nor recognize truth to seek it or falsehood to avoid it. (al-Tanbih wa'l-Ashraf: 198, chapter on the history from the birth of the Messenger.)

He said: Many people went to the view that he had never associated anything with Allah, and so he did not need to renew Islam. (Muruj al-Dhahab: 2/400, Cairo ed. 1346 AH; Beirut ed. 2/276, chapter on his mission and what came of it until his migration.)

Al-Maqrizi said: As for Ali, he never associated partners with Allah at all. When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he informed Khadija, and she affirmed it, he and Ali were together. Ali did not need to be called, nor was he a polytheist who would then need to be made a monotheist so that it could be said he "embraced Islam." This is the verified position. (Imta' al-Asma': 1/16-17, edited by Mahmud Shakir, Cairo ed.)

Something similar is related from al-Amiri. (al-Riyad al-Mustabata: 168, his biography.)

Abu Ja'far al-Iskafi said, after mentioning the hadith of the house: Would a child who is not discerning and not sensible be charged with preparing the food and calling the people? Would a child be entrusted with the secret of prophethood? Would anyone be counted among the elders and the grown men except an intelligent and judicious person? Would the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) place his hand in his, and give him the handshake of allegiance, with the promise of the brotherhood, the bequest and the caliphate, unless he were fit for that? He who had reached the limit of responsibility, who could bear the guardianship of Allah and the enmity of His enemies. What is it with this child who did not become attached to his peers, did not join those of his kind, and was not seen among the boys in their games after his Islam?

Rather, we have seen him only persisting in his Islam, resolute in his affair, making his word true by his deed. He confirmed his Islam through his chastity and asceticism, and he clung to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more than anyone present.

He (peace be upon him) also mentioned in his speeches and sermons the beginning of his condition and the opening of his affair, when he embraced Islam when the Messenger of Allah called the tree, and it came toward him dragging along the earth. Quraysh said: "A sorcerer, a great sorcerer."

Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am the first to believe in you. I believed in Allah and His Messenger, and I affirmed you in what you brought. I bear witness that the tree did what it did by the command of Allah, as confirmation of your prophethood and as proof of your call."

Could there ever be a faith more sound than this faith? More firm in its bond and more steadfast in its strength? But the bias of the Uthmaniyya, their rage, the partisanship of al-Jahiz and his deviation are things with no remedy. (Sharh al-Nahj: 13/244, sermon 238; and al-Ghadir: 2/287, citing his book 'Ala al-Uthmaniyya.)

(Ali was the first to embrace Islam) Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said in al-Isti'ab: It is related from Salman, Abu Dhar, al-Miqdad, Khabbab, Jabir, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Zayd ibn Arqam that "Ali ibn Abi Talib was the first to embrace Islam," and these preferred him over others.
