He said: meaning, "wait for us."

﴿That we may borrow from your light﴾: that is, that we may be illuminated by your light. The commentators said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, exalted is He, gives the believers light according to the measure of their deeds, and they walk by it upon the Ṣirāṭ. He also gives the hypocrites and the misguided the same, as a deception for them, and this is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And He is their deceiver﴾ [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 142].

Al-Kalbī said: Rather, the hypocrites are illuminated by the light of the believers, and they are not given light themselves. [Al-Tashīl li-ʿUlūm al-Tanzīl: 4/96.]

They said: So while they were walking, Allah sent a wind and darkness, and the light of the hypocrites was extinguished. That is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us; indeed You are over all things competent."﴾ They fear that their light might be taken away as the hypocrites' light was taken away. So when the hypocrites remain in darkness, they say to the believers: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.﴾ It is said: ﴿Return you behind you; then seek light﴾, that is, go back to the place from which you came and seek there for yourselves light, for there is no way for you to borrow from our light. ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾ — a wall (sūr); the bāʾ is extra, according to al-Kisāʾī. It is a barrier between Paradise and Hellfire. ﴿Within it is mercy﴾, meaning Paradise; ﴿and without it, from the direction of it, is torment﴾, meaning the Fire.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Aḥmad ibn Mā/ja al-Qazwīnī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb al-Rāzī related to us: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us. And Ibn Ḥamdān informed me: Ibn Māhān related to us: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us: Ḥammād, from Abū Sinān, who said: I was with ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās at the Valley of Hell, and he narrated from his father, and he recited ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾ up to the end of the verse. Then he said: "This is the place of the wall," meaning the Valley of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sunnī related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿUmayr ibn Yūsuf informed me: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAtīq related to us: Abū Muṣhir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from ʿAṭiyyah ibn Qays, who said: Abū al-ʿAwwām, the muezzin of the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, told me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The wall that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, mentioned in the Qur'an, ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door, within it is mercy and without it, from the direction of it, is torment﴾, is the eastern wall of the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis; its inner side is from the mosque, and its outer side from the direction of it is torment: the valley, which is the Valley of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me: al-Sunnī related to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī related to us: Abū Naṣr al-Tammār related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ziyād ibn Abī Sawdah, that ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit stood upon the eastern wall of Bayt al-Maqdis and wept. Some of them said: "What makes you weep, Abū al-Walīd?" He said: "From here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us that he saw Hell."

ʿAqīl informed me that Abū al-Faraj related to them, from Muḥammad ibn Jarīr, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf related to me: Abū al-Mughīrah related to us: Ṣafwān related to us: Shurayḥ related to us that Kaʿb said, concerning the gate called the Gate of Mercy in Bayt al-Maqdis, that it is the gate about which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾, the verse.

﴿They will call out to them﴾, meaning the hypocrites call out to the believers when the wall has been placed between them, so they remain in darkness and torment, while the believers are in light and mercy: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾ in the world, fasting, praying, marrying you and inheriting from you? ﴿They will say: "Yes, but you tempted yourselves, and you waited, and you doubted, and desires deceived you, until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah."﴾ ﴿You tempted yourselves﴾: you destroyed yourselves with hypocrisy. ﴿And you waited﴾: with faith.

Muqātil said: Rather, you waited for Muḥammad's death, and you said: "Muḥammad will soon die, so we will be at rest." ﴿And you doubted﴾: you were skeptical about monotheism and prophethood. ﴿And desires deceived you﴾: by false hopes.

Abū Bakr al-Warrāq said: It is long hope (ṭūl al-amal).

Al-Ḥusayn informed me: Ibn Ḥamdān related to us: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Muslim ibn Adham related to us: Hammām ibn Yaḥyā related to us: Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew lines, and drew one line to the side and said: "Do you know what this is? This is the likeness of the son of Adam and the likeness of wishful desire, and that line is hope. While he is wishing, death comes to him." [219] [Fatḥ al-Bārī: 11/203; and Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 17/247.]

And al-Ḥusayn informed us: al-Kindī related to us: Abū ʿĪsā Ḥamzah ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar related to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Bilāl ibn Saʿd, who said: Remembering your good deeds and forgetting your bad deeds is deception.

﴿Until the command of Allah came﴾, meaning death. ﴿And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah﴾, that is, Satan. Samāk ibn Ḥarb recited (al-Ghurūr) with a ḍammah on the ghayn, meaning the false things.

Qatādah said: They were under the deception of Satan, and they remained under it until Allah cast them into the Fire.

﴿So today, no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾: a substitute and an exchange. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire﴾: that is, it is your companion and more deserving of you, and more fitting to be your dwelling. ﴿It is your master, and wretched is the destination.﴾

Labīd said:

"So He punishes both groups according to what is due:
He is the master of fear, its creator and its leader."

[Al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2529.]

﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth?﴾ The verse. Al-Kalbī and Muqātil said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, a year after the Hijrah, for they once asked Salmān al-Fārisī, saying: "Tell us about what is in the Torah, for it has marvels." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif, Lām, Rā. These are the verses of the clear Book … We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Sūrat Yūsuf: 3]. So He informed them that this Qur'an is better than other things and more beneficial for them. They ceased asking Salmān for as long as Allah willed, then [returned] [In the manuscript: "a'adū" (they returned).] and asked Salmān about the like of that, and the verse was revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾, the verse [Sūrat al-Zumar: 23].

They ceased asking Salmān for as long as Allah willed, then [returned] again and asked, saying: "Tell us about the Torah, for it has marvels," and this verse was revealed.

According to this view, the interpretation of the verse ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe﴾ refers to openness and tongue (i.e., overt speech).

Others said: It was revealed concerning the believers.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew weary, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would tell us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾, the verse.

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would relate to us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾, the verse.

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would remind us and admonish us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Masʿūd said: Between our Islam and the time we were rebuked with this verse there were only four years, so the believers began to rebuke one another.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah, exalted is He, found the believers' hearts slow, so He rebuked them at the end of thirteen years from the revelation of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Has the time not come (yaʾni, yaḥinn) for those who believe that their hearts should humble (takhshaʿa) — be softened, be gentle, and submit — before the remembrance of Allah?﴾

Shaybah, Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim, according to the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal and Ḥafṣ, recited (nazzala) with a light zāy; others recited it with a shadda.

﴿Of the truth﴾, which is the Qur'an. Mujāhid said: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouins who became nomads after the Hijrah.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us: Muḥammad ibn Khālid related to us: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd related to us: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yazīd ibn Hārūn related to us: al-Ḥusām ibn al-Muṣakk [In some books of biography: Ḥusām ibn Muṣakk, with the alif and lām removed; see Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb: 2/213, no. 446.] related to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Shaddād ibn Aws, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing to be lifted from people is humility." [220] [Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 2/136; and al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr: 7/295.]

﴿And let them not be﴾: meaning, and that they not be, its position being in the accusative by coordination with (takhshaʿa). Al-Akhfash said: If you wish, you may make it a prohibition, so its sense is: "And let them not be," and the evidence for this interpretation is the transmission of Yūnus from Yaʿqūb, that he recited (wa-lā takūnū) with a tāʾ.

﴿Like those who were given the Book before, then the term grew long for them, and their hearts hardened.﴾ Those are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾: the time, the age, and the duration between them and their prophets. ﴿So their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

ʿAmmār ibn ʿUmayr related, from al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿUmaylah, from al-Aʿmash, who said: "ʿAbd Allāh related to us, I have not heard a better narration than it, except the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, or a narration from the Prophet (ﷺ)," that the Children of Israel, when the term grew long for them, their hearts hardened, and they invented a book from their own selves, which their hearts inclined to and their souls made lawful, while the truth used to stand between them and many of their desires, until they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know. They said: "Present this book to the Children of Israel: if they follow you, leave them alone; and if they oppose you, kill them." Then they said: "No, rather send for so-and-so, a man of their scholars, and present the book to him: if he follows you, no one will oppose you after him; and if he opposes you, kill him, and none will disagree with you after him."

They sent for him, and he took a sheet and wrote the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, on it, then placed it in a horn (qarn), then hung it on his neck, then put clothes over it. Then he came to them, and they presented the book to him and said: "Do you believe in this?" He pointed to his chest and said: "I believe in this. And why should I not believe in this?" meaning the book in the horn. So they let him go.

He had companions who used to visit him, and when he died they dug him up and found the horn, and they found the Book in it. They said: "Do you not see his saying: 'I believe in this, and why should I not believe in this?' He only meant this book." Then the Children of Israel disagreed into some seventy sects, and the best of their sects were the people of Dhū al-Qarn.

ʿAbd Allāh said: Whoever among you remains will see an evil, and in accordance with my command he will see an evil that he cannot change; let him know that Allah knows in his heart that he hates it.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: This refers only to the believers among the People of the Book before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾: meaning the emergence of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿So their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾: meaning those who innovated monasticism, the people of the monasteries. A group of them remained firm upon the religion of ʿĪsā until the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, and they believed in him; and among them is a group that turned back from their religion, and these are the ones who were declared defiant, so they disbelieved in the religion of ʿĪsā and did not believe in Muḥammad (peace be upon him).

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: The Companions in Mecca were in hardship, and when they emigrated they obtained fertile land and comfort, and they slackened from what they had been in, so their hearts hardened. Therefore the believers should increase in faith, certainty and sincerity through long companionship with the Book.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Ḍabbī informed us: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nayyirī informed us: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashaj related to us: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar related to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from Wā'il ibn Bakr, who said: ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) said: "Do not multiply speech without the remembrance of Allah, lest your hearts harden, for the hard heart is far from Allah, but you do not know. And do not look into the sins of people as though you were lords; look into your own sins as though you were servants, for people are only of two kinds: the afflicted and the safe. So have mercy on the people of affliction, and praise Allah for well-being." [221]

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā informed us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Muqriʾ related to us, saying: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī say: I heard Abū ʿAmmār al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth say: I heard al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā al-Sīnānī say: The cause of al-Faḍl ibn ʿIyāḍ's repentance was that he fell in love with a slave girl, and she arranged a rendezvous with him at night. While he was climbing the walls toward her, he heard a reciter reciting: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah﴾, so he turned back backward.

He was saying: "Yes, so-and-so, yes, by Allah, so-and-so." Then the night brought him to a ruin, in which there was a group of travelers, and suddenly some of them were saying to others in Persian: "Fuḍayl has come upon us on the road; now he will be on guard."

Fuḍayl said to himself: "Do I not see myself striving in the night toward sins, while a people among the Muslims fear me?"

"O Allah, I have indeed repented to You, and I have made my repentance to You a neighborhood of Your Sacred House."

Then he turned toward them and said to them in Persian: "You feared me, Fuḍayl, for I am a sinner; now fear [Allah]."

Al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā said: Then he went out and settled in Mecca.

Abū Saʿd ibn Abī ʿUthmān al-Zāhid related to us: Abū al-Faḍl Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿImrān informed us in Mecca: Abū Yaʿqūb al-Bazzāz related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim al-Samarqandī related to us: Aḥmad ibn Zayd related to us: Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubārak was asked, while I was present, about the beginning of his asceticism, and he said: "I was in an orchard when I was young, with a group of my peers, and that was at the time of the fruits. We ate and drank, and I was devoted to playing the lute. I got up in the middle of the night, and suddenly a branch was moving by my head. I took the lute to strike it, but the lute spoke, saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah﴾." He said: "I struck the lute against the ground and broke it, and I turned away from everything I had been engaged in that had occupied me from Allah. Then the success of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, came, and what was made easy for us of good was by the grace of Allah."

﴿On the Day you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands.﴾

Some of them said: He meant all their sides, so He expressed the part for the whole, in keeping with the Arab practice of brevity (ījāz). Its figurative sense is: "on their right sides."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He meant ﴿their light running before them and on their right hands﴾ as their books.

Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī recited ﴿bi-īmānihim﴾ with a kasra on the hamza. The sound recitation (al-qirāʾah al-ṣaḥīḥah) is what the common readers hold to. He meant by the light: the Qur'an.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: They are given their light according to the measure of their deeds. Among them is one whose light comes like a palm tree, and among them is one whose light is given like a standing man, and the least of them in light has it on his big toe; it is extinguished at one moment and kindled at another.

Qatādah said: It was related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the believers is one whose light shines from Madinah to ʿAdan Abyan and Ṣanʿāʾ and beyond that, and among the believers is one whose light does not illuminate the place of his feet." And the angels will say to them: ﴿Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ [218] [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/330.]

﴿On the Day the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed: "Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light."﴾ The common readers recite it as a wasl form, i.e., "wait for us" (intaẓirūnā).

Yahya, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamzah recited (anẓirūnā) with a fatḥah on the alif and a kasra on the ẓāʾ, meaning "give us respite" (amhilūnā).

Al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs say: anẓirnī, meaning "wait for me" (intaẓirnī). He cited in this regard the verse of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:

"O Abā Hind, do not hasten against us,
and wait for us, and we will inform you with certainty."

[Commentary on the Seven Mu'allaqat: 117.]

He said: meaning, "wait for us."

﴿That we may borrow from your light﴾: that is, that we may be illuminated by your light. The commentators said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, exalted is He, gives the believers light according to the measure of their deeds, and they walk by it upon the Ṣirāṭ. He also gives the hypocrites and the misguided the same, as a deception for them, and this is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And He is their deceiver﴾ [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 142].

Al-Kalbī said: Rather, the hypocrites are illuminated by the light of the believers, and they are not given light themselves. [Al-Tashīl li-ʿUlūm al-Tanzīl: 4/96.]

They said: So while they were walking, Allah sent a wind and darkness, and the light of the hypocrites was extinguished. That is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us; indeed You are over all things competent."﴾ They fear that their light might be taken away as the hypocrites' light was taken away. So when the hypocrites remain in darkness, they say to the believers: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.﴾ It is said: ﴿Return you behind you; then seek light﴾, that is, go back to the place from which you came and seek there for yourselves light, for there is no way for you to borrow from our light. ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾ — a wall (sūr); the bāʾ is extra, according to al-Kisāʾī. It is a barrier between Paradise and Hellfire. ﴿Within it is mercy﴾, meaning Paradise; ﴿and without it, from the direction of it, is torment﴾, meaning the Fire.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Aḥmad ibn Mā/ja al-Qazwīnī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb al-Rāzī related to us: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us. And Ibn Ḥamdān informed me: Ibn Māhān related to us: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl related to us: Ḥammād, from Abū Sinān, who said: I was with ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās at the Valley of Hell, and he narrated from his father, and he recited ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾ up to the end of the verse. Then he said: "This is the place of the wall," meaning the Valley of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sunnī related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿUmayr ibn Yūsuf informed me: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAtīq related to us: Abū Muṣhir related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from ʿAṭiyyah ibn Qays, who said: Abū al-ʿAwwām, the muezzin of the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, told me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The wall that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, mentioned in the Qur'an, ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door, within it is mercy and without it, from the direction of it, is torment﴾, is the eastern wall of the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis; its inner side is from the mosque, and its outer side from the direction of it is torment: the valley, which is the Valley of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me: al-Sunnī related to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī related to us: Abū Naṣr al-Tammār related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us, from Ziyād ibn Abī Sawdah, that ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit stood upon the eastern wall of Bayt al-Maqdis and wept. Some of them said: "What makes you weep, Abū al-Walīd?" He said: "From here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us that he saw Hell."

ʿAqīl informed me that Abū al-Faraj related to them, from Muḥammad ibn Jarīr, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf related to me: Abū al-Mughīrah related to us: Ṣafwān related to us: Shurayḥ related to us that Kaʿb said, concerning the gate called the Gate of Mercy in Bayt al-Maqdis, that it is the gate about which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a door﴾, the verse.

﴿They will call out to them﴾, meaning the hypocrites call out to the believers when the wall has been placed between them, so they remain in darkness and torment, while the believers are in light and mercy: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾ in the world, fasting, praying, marrying you and inheriting from you? ﴿They will say: "Yes, but you tempted yourselves, and you waited, and you doubted, and desires deceived you, until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah."﴾ ﴿You tempted yourselves﴾: you destroyed yourselves with hypocrisy. ﴿And you waited﴾: with faith.

This is the likeness of the son of Adam and the likeness of wishful desire, and that line is hope. While he is wishing, death comes to him." [219] [Fatḥ al-Bārī: 11/203; and Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 17/247.]

And al-Ḥusayn informed us: al-Kindī related to us: Abū ʿĪsā Ḥamzah ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar related to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān related to us: al-Walīd ibn Muslim related to us, from al-Awzāʿī, from Bilāl ibn Saʿd, who said: Remembering your good deeds and forgetting your bad deeds is deception.

﴿Until the command of Allah came﴾, meaning death. ﴿And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah﴾, that is, Satan. Samāk ibn Ḥarb recited (al-Ghurūr) with a ḍammah on the ghayn, meaning the false things.

Qatādah said: They were under the deception of Satan, and they remained under it until Allah cast them into the Fire.

﴿So today, no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾: a substitute and an exchange. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire﴾: that is, it is your companion and more deserving of you, and more fitting to be your dwelling. ﴿It is your master, and wretched is the destination.﴾

Labīd said:

"So He punishes both groups according to what is due:
He is the master of fear, its creator and its leader."

[Al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2529.]

﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth?﴾ The verse. Al-Kalbī and Muqātil said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, a year after the Hijrah, for they once asked Salmān al-Fārisī, saying: "Tell us about what is in the Torah, for it has marvels." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Alif, Lām, Rā. These are the verses of the clear Book … We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Sūrat Yūsuf: 3]. So He informed them that this Qur'an is better than other things and more beneficial for them. They ceased asking Salmān for as long as Allah willed, then [returned] [In the manuscript: "a'adū" (they returned).] and asked Salmān about the like of that, and the verse was revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾, the verse [Sūrat al-Zumar: 23].

They ceased asking Salmān for as long as Allah willed, then [returned] again and asked, saying: "Tell us about the Torah, for it has marvels," and this verse was revealed.

According to this view, the interpretation of the verse ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe﴾ refers to openness and tongue (i.e., overt speech).

Others said: It was revealed concerning the believers.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew weary, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would tell us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾, the verse.

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would relate to us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾, the verse.

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would remind us and admonish us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Masʿūd said: Between our Islam and the time we were rebuked with this verse there were only four years, so the believers began to rebuke one another.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah, exalted is He, found the believers' hearts slow, so He rebuked them at the end of thirteen years from the revelation of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Has the time not come (yaʾni, yaḥinn) for those who believe that their hearts should humble (takhshaʿa) — be softened, be gentle, and submit — before the remembrance of Allah?﴾

Shaybah, Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim, according to the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal and Ḥafṣ, recited (nazzala) with a light zāy; others recited it with a shadda.

﴿Of the truth﴾, which is the Qur'an. Mujāhid said: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouins who became nomads after the Hijrah.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us: Muḥammad ibn Khālid related to us: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd related to us: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yazīd ibn Hārūn related to us: al-Ḥusām ibn al-Muṣakk [In some books of biography: Ḥusām ibn Muṣakk, with the alif and lām removed; see Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb: 2/213, no. 446.] related to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Shaddād ibn Aws, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing to be lifted from people is humility." [220] [Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 2/136; and al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr: 7/295.]

﴿And let them not be﴾: meaning, and that they not be, its position being in the accusative by coordination with (takhshaʿa). Al-Akhfash said: If you wish, you may make it a prohibition, so its sense is: "And let them not be," and the evidence for this interpretation is the transmission of Yūnus from Yaʿqūb, that he recited (wa-lā takūnū) with a tāʾ.

﴿Like those who were given the Book before, then the term grew long for them, and their hearts hardened.﴾ Those are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾: the time, the age, and the duration between them and their prophets. ﴿So their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

ʿAmmār ibn ʿUmayr related, from al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿUmaylah, from al-Aʿmash, who said: "ʿAbd Allāh related to us, I have not heard a better narration than it, except the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, or a narration from the Prophet (ﷺ)," that the Children of Israel, when the term grew long for them, their hearts hardened, and they invented a book from their own selves, which their hearts inclined to and their souls made lawful, while the truth used to stand between them and many of their desires, until they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know. They said: "Present this book to the Children of Israel: if they follow you, leave them alone; and if they oppose you, kill them." Then they said: "No, rather send for so-and-so, a man of their scholars, and present the book to him: if he follows you, no one will oppose you after him; and if he opposes you, kill him, and none will disagree with you after him."

They sent for him, and he took a sheet and wrote the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, on it, then placed it in a horn (qarn), then hung it on his neck, then put clothes over it. Then he came to them, and they presented the book to him and said: "Do you believe in this?" He pointed to his chest and said: "I believe in this. And why should I not believe in this?" meaning the book in the horn. So they let him go.

He had companions who used to visit him, and when he died they dug him up and found the horn, and they found the Book in it. They said: "Do you not see his saying: 'I believe in this, and why should I not believe in this?' He only meant this book." Then the Children of Israel disagreed into some seventy sects, and the best of their sects were the people of Dhū al-Qarn.

ʿAbd Allāh said: Whoever among you remains will see an evil, and in accordance with my command he will see an evil that he cannot change; let him know that Allah knows in his heart that he hates it.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: This refers only to the believers among the People of the Book before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾: meaning the emergence of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿So their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾: meaning those who innovated monasticism, the people of the monasteries. A group of them remained firm upon the religion of ʿĪsā until the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, and they believed in him; and among them is a group that turned back from their religion, and these are the ones who were declared defiant, so they disbelieved in the religion of ʿĪsā and did not believe in Muḥammad (peace be upon him).

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: The Companions in Mecca were in hardship, and when they emigrated they obtained fertile land and comfort, and they slackened from what they had been in, so their hearts hardened. Therefore the believers should increase in faith, certainty and sincerity through long companionship with the Book.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Ḍabbī informed us: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nayyirī informed us: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashaj related to us: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar related to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from Wā'il ibn Bakr, who said: ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) said: "Do not multiply speech without the remembrance of Allah, lest your hearts harden, for the hard heart is far from Allah, but you do not know. And do not look into the sins of people as though you were lords; look into your own sins as though you were servants, for people are only of two kinds: the afflicted and the safe. So have mercy on the people of affliction, and praise Allah for well-being." [221]

Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā informed us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Muqriʾ related to us, saying: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī say: I heard Abū ʿAmmār al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth say: I heard al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā al-Sīnānī say: The cause of al-Faḍl ibn ʿIyāḍ's repentance was that he fell in love with a slave girl, and she arranged a rendezvous with him at night. While he was climbing the walls toward her, he heard a reciter reciting: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah﴾, so he turned back backward.

He was saying: "Yes, so-and-so, yes, by Allah, so-and-so." Then the night brought him to a ruin, in which there was a group of travelers, and suddenly some of them were saying to others in Persian: "Fuḍayl has come upon us on the road; now he will be on guard."

Fuḍayl said to himself: "Do I not see myself striving in the night toward sins, while a people among the Muslims fear me?"

"O Allah, I have indeed repented to You, and I have made my repentance to You a neighborhood of Your Sacred House."

Then he turned toward them and said to them in Persian: "You feared me, Fuḍayl, for I am a sinner; now fear [Allah]."

Al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā said: Then he went out and settled in Mecca.

Abū Saʿd ibn Abī ʿUthmān al-Zāhid related to us: Abū al-Faḍl Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿImrān informed us in Mecca: Abū Yaʿqūb al-Bazzāz related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim al-Samarqandī related to us: Aḥmad ibn Zayd related to us: Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubārak was asked, while I was present, about the beginning of his asceticism, and he said: "I was in an orchard when I was young, with a group of my peers, and that was at the time of the fruits. We ate and drank, and I was devoted to playing the lute. I got up in the middle of the night, and suddenly a branch was moving by my head. I took the lute to strike it, but the lute spoke, saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah﴾." He said: "I struck the lute against the ground and broke it, and I turned away from everything I had been engaged in that had occupied me from Allah. Then the success of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, came, and what was made easy for us of good was by the grace of Allah."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 57, verses 17–25:

﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have made the signs clear to you, so that you may use your reason.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the men who give in charity (al-mussaddiqin) and the women who give in charity (al-mussaddiqat)...﴾ Ibn Kathir, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read the two sad (ص) with a single consonant (تخفيف), from taṣdīq (affirming). Its meaning is: "Indeed, the believing men and the believing women."

The rest of the readers read them with doubling (تشديد), meaning "those who give charity" (al-mutaṣaddiqin and al-mutaṣaddiqat). The tā' was assimilated into the ṣād, as in al-Muzzammil and al-Muddaththir. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Ḥātim preferred this reading, in view of the reading of Ubayy: "Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and who lend to Allah a goodly loan," meaning by charity and expenditure in His way.

Al-Ḥasan said: "Everything in the Qur'an concerning the goodly loan is voluntary (taṭawwuʿ) giving." The verb was joined to the noun because it is in the sense of a verb. Its meaning: "Indeed, those who gave charity and lent to Allah, it will be multiplied for them many times over."

The common recitation is with an alif and with a fatḥa on the ʿayn (يُضاعِفُ). Al-Aʿmash read (يُضاعِفُه) with a kasra on the ʿayn and an added pronoun hā'.

Ibn ʿĀmir, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʿfar read (يُضَعِّف) with doubling.

﴿And they will have a generous reward﴾, which is Paradise.

﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful (al-ṣiddīqūn)﴾. Its singular is ṣiddīq, meaning one who is very truthful.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "They are eight men who preceded the people of the earth in their time to Islam: Abu Bakr, ʿAlī, Zayd, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿd, and Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. The ninth of them was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, whom Allah joined with them because of what He knew of the sincerity of His Prophet."

﴿And the martyrs are with their Lord﴾. The scholars differed concerning the structure (naẓm) and the ruling of this verse. One group said: the sentence is complete at His words "the truthful," and then a new beginning: "and the martyrs." By this they meant only the martyrs among the believers. The wāw here is the wāw of exception (istithnāʾ). This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Masrūq, and a group of scholars.

Others said: it is connected to what comes before it, and the wāw here is the wāw of coordination (nasaq).

Then they differed about its meaning. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it was revealed concerning specific people among the believers, all of whom were martyrs, and their mention has already passed.

Another said: it was revealed concerning all the sincere believers.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me, by licence, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghannām al-Nakhaʿī narrated to us, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Abu Qays, from al-Hurmul, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "A man fights people so that his position may be seen. A man fights for worldly gain. A man fights seeking the face of Allah. And a man dies on his bed and is a martyr." Then he recited: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord.﴾

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid also informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Khālid informed us, saying: Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn Layth narrated to us, from Mujāhid, who said: "Every believer is a truthful one and a martyr." Then he recited this verse, meaning as a connected reading.

Ibn ʿAbbās said in some narrations: by "the martyrs" he meant only the prophets.

﴿They will have their reward and their light﴾ in the darkness of the Resurrection. ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾

﴿Know that the life of this world is﴾: (mā) is a supplementary particle (ṣila). Its meaning: "Know ..."

﴿Mere play﴾: vain, having no outcome. ﴿And amusement﴾: joy that then passes away. ﴿And adornment﴾: an appearance by which people adorn themselves. ﴿And boasting among you﴾: that some of you boast about to others. ﴿And rivalry in wealth and children﴾: that is, to be proud of the abundance of wealth and children.

Some later commentators said: "Play like the play of children, amusement like the amusement of youths, adornment like the adornment of women, boasting like the boasting of rivals, and rivalry like the rivalry of the landed notables (dihqān)."

ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭālib said to ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir: "Do not grieve over the world, for the world is six things: food, drink, clothing, scent, mount, and marriage. Its greatest food is honey, and it is the vomit of a fly. Its greatest drink is water, which all living things share. Its greatest clothing is brocade, and it is the spun thread of a worm. Its greatest scent is musk, and it is the blood of a gazelle's musk-gland. Its greatest mount is the horse, and on it men are killed. Its greatest marriage is women, and it is urine upon urine. By Allah, a woman adorns her best so that what is meant is her worst."

Then Allah, mighty is His remembrance, struck a parable for it, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Like rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers. Then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow, then it becomes debris.﴾ That is, the farmers. Then it decays and perishes. ﴿And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness﴾, meaning: or forgiveness ﴿from Allah, and pleasure. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾

﴿Race (sāriʿū) to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Its breadth (ʿarḍ): its vastness, like the breadth of the heavens and the earth, if they were joined together.

Ibn Kaysān said: it means one single garden among the gardens.

﴿Prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of mighty bounty.﴾ ﴿No misfortune befalls on the earth, nor in yourselves﴾, through drought, famine, the loss of crops and fruit, nor through ailments and sicknesses.

Al-Shaʿbī said: "Misfortune" refers to whatever occurs of good and evil, what grieves and what pleases.

The evidence for this interpretation is His words, Glorified is He: ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you﴾, so He mentioned both states together.

﴿Except that it is in a Book﴾, meaning the Preserved Tablet, ﴿before We bring it into being﴾: before We create the earth and the souls.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means the misfortune itself.

Abu al-ʿĀliya said: it means the soul (nasma).

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ That is, creating it and preserving it is easy for Allah.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Makhlad informed us, saying: Dāwūd informed us, saying: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: al-Rabīʿ ibn Abi Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: "I entered upon Saʿīd ibn Jubayr with a group of people, and a man among the people wept. He said: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'I weep for what I see of you, and for what is taking you to it.' He said: 'Do not weep, for it was in the knowledge of Allah, Glorified is He, that it would happen. Have you not heard the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿No misfortune befalls on the earth nor in yourselves﴾ ...' the verse."

﴿So that you do not grieve﴾: be sad ﴿over what has escaped you﴾ of the world, ﴿and do not exult﴾: be arrogant ﴿over what He has given you.﴾ The recitation of the majority is with an extended alif, meaning "gave you" (aʿṭākum), and this was preferred by Abu Ḥātim. Abu ʿAmr read with a short alif, meaning "came to you" (jāʾakum), and this was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd, who said: "Because of His words, Glorified is He: (fātakum), and He did not say (afātakum). So He made the verb belong to Himself, and similarly (atākum) makes the verb belong to Him, so that the speech agrees with its parts."

ʿIkrima said: "There is no one who does not rejoice and grieve. So make your joy gratitude and your grief patience."

﴿And Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾: one who is proud of what has been given to him of the world, boasting about it over people.

Ibn Masʿūd said: "The feeling of a burning coal, which burns what it burns and leaves what it leaves, is dearer to me than to say of something that happened: 'I wish it had not happened,' or of something that did not happen: 'I wish it had happened.'"

Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: "O son of Adam, why do you grieve over a lost thing which death will not return to you? And why do you rejoice in a present thing which death will not leave in your hands?"

It was said to Buzurjmihr: "Why, O wise one, do you not grieve over what has passed, nor rejoice over what is coming?" He said: "Because what has passed cannot be recovered by regret, and what is coming cannot be kept by delight."

Al-Fuḍayl said on this meaning: "The world is one that gives benefit and one that destroys. What it destroys has no return, and what it benefits has announced departure."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "By this verse Allah has bound the believers to the bitter endurance of patience over what has passed, the abandonment of exultation over what comes, and contentment with His decree in both states."

Qutayba ibn Saʿīd said: "I entered one of the Arab tribal settlements, and there I saw an open land filled with dead camels and carcasses, in a number I could not count. I asked an old woman: 'To whom did these camels belong?' She pointed to an old man on a hill spinning wool. I said to him: 'O old man, were these camels yours?' He said: 'They were in my name.' I said: 'What happened to them?' He said: 'He who gave them has taken them back.' I said: 'Did you say anything about that?' He said: 'Yes:

No, by He who took [...] from His creation,
and man in this age is a target of calamity and trials.
I am not glad that my camels are in their pastures,
and what is decreed by Allah has not been otherwise.'"

Salm al-Khawwāṣ said: "Whoever wants to eat of both abodes, let him enter our way for two years, so that Allah places this world and the next before him." It was asked: "And what is your way?" He said: "Contentment with the decree, and opposing desire."

And he recited:

Do not prolong grief over what has passed,
for grief rarely benefits you.
Equal is one who grieves over what has gone,
and one who shows grief over what has not happened.

﴿Those who are miserly﴾: it is said that it is in the genitive case as a description of "the arrogant boaster." It is also said that it is in the nominative as the subject of an inceptive sentence, whose predicate is what follows. ﴿And they command people to be miserly. And whoever turns away, then indeed Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.﴾ The people of Madina and Syria read without the pronoun "huwa," and it is so in their codices. The rest read it with the pronoun.

﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾, meaning the scale, by which one acts justly. Ibn Zayd said: "It is that by which things are weighed."

﴿That mankind may uphold justice﴾: that people may deal justly among themselves.

﴿And We sent down iron﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Adam descended from Paradise with five iron tools: the anvil, the tongs, the pincers, the hammer, and the needle."

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means that He brought forth iron for them from the mines, and taught them its craft through His revelation.

Qutrub said: "This is from the sense of provision (nuzl), as you say: 'He provided for so-and-so a goodly provision (nuzlan ḥasanan).' So the meaning of the verse is that He made that a provision for them. Similar is His words: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of cattle﴾."

The evidence for the interpretation of the early exegetes is what:

Abu Sufyān al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Dihqān informed us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Khalaf al-Khayyāṭ narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj al-Muʿaddil narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn Muḥammad Abu Muḥammad (son of the sister of Sufyān al-Thawrī) narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Malik al-Tamīmī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khalīfa, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down four blessings from the sky to the earth: He sent down iron, fire, water, and salt."

﴿In it is mighty violence﴾, a great strength, meaning weapons and horses, ﴿and benefits for mankind﴾, by which they use it for their interests and livelihoods, since it is the instrument of every craft. ﴿And that Allah may know﴾, meaning: We sent Our messengers and sent down these things with them, ﴿so that people may deal with truth and justice, and that Allah may see who helps Him﴾, that is, His religion, ﴿and His messengers, unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾

﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾, meaning the scale, by which one acts justly. Ibn Zayd said: "It is that by which things are weighed."

﴿That mankind may uphold justice﴾: that people may deal justly among themselves.

﴿And We sent down iron﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Adam descended from Paradise with five iron tools: the anvil, the tongs, the pincers, the hammer, and the needle."

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means that He brought forth iron for them from the mines, and taught them its craft through His revelation.

Qutrub said: "This is from the sense of provision (nuzl), as you say: 'He provided for so-and-so a goodly provision (nuzlan ḥasanan).' So the meaning of the verse is that He made that a provision for them. Similar is His words: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of cattle﴾."

The evidence for the interpretation of the early exegetes is what:

Abu Sufyān al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Dihqān informed us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Khalaf al-Khayyāṭ narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj al-Muʿaddil narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn Muḥammad Abu Muḥammad (son of the sister of Sufyān al-Thawrī) narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Malik al-Tamīmī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khalīfa, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down four blessings from the sky to the earth: He sent down iron, fire, water, and salt."

﴿In it is mighty violence﴾, a great strength, meaning weapons and horses, ﴿and benefits for mankind﴾, by which they use it for their interests and livelihoods, since it is the instrument of every craft. ﴿And that Allah may know﴾, meaning: We sent Our messengers and sent down these things with them, ﴿so that people may deal with truth and justice, and that Allah may see who helps Him﴾, that is, His religion, ﴿and His messengers, unseen. **Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 57, verses 26–29:**

﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture. So among them is one who is guided, but many of them are defiant transgressors. Then We followed up after them with Our messengers, and We followed up with Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. And monasticism (rahbaniyya), which they invented themselves, We did not prescribe for them; they only sought the pleasure of God. But they did not observe it with its proper observance. So We gave those of them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiant transgressors.﴾

*Al-ra'fa* is the most intense tenderness. *Rahbaniyya* (monasticism) they invented from themselves. *Ma katabnaha* means "We did not prescribe it," that is, "We did not make it obligatory upon them." *Illa ibtighaa'* means: "But they sought," that is, "rather they sought the pleasure of God through that monasticism." *Fa-ataynaa alladhina amanu minhum ajrahum*: these are the people of compassion and mercy, and the monasticism they invented in pursuit of God's pleasure. *Wa katheerun minhum fasiqoon* refers to those who did not uphold monasticism as it should be upheld, who disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, and who became Jews or Christians.

Traditions have been transmitted in accordance with what we have explained.

Ibn Mas'ud said: I was riding behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on a donkey, and he said to me: "O son of Umm 'Abd, do you know from where the Children of Israel took up monasticism?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Tyrants prevailed over them after Jesus (peace be upon him), acting in disobedience to God the Glorified. The people of faith became angry and fought them, and the people of faith were defeated three times, until only a few of them remained. They said: 'If we prevail over these people, they will annihilate us, and no one will be left to call to the religion.' So let us disperse in the earth until God sends the Prophet whom Jesus promised us,' meaning Muhammad. So they dispersed into the caves of the mountains and innovated monasticism. Some of them held fast to their religion, and some of them disbelieved." Then he recited this verse: *"And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them"*, to the end of the verse.

*Fa-ataynaa alladhina amanu minhum*, meaning: those who remained steadfast in it, *ajrahum*. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O son of Umm 'Abd, do you know what the monasticism of my community is?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "Emigration, jihad, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, the 'umra, and glorifying God (takbir) on the hilltops." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/265.]] [224]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Muzani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Shayban ibn Farrukh told us, saying: al-Sa'q ibn Hazn told us, from 'Aqil al-Ja'di, from Abu Ishaq, from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "O son of Mas'ud, those who were before you split into seventy-two sects, and three of them were saved while the rest perished. One sect confronted the kings and fought them over the religion of Jesus, and they seized them and killed them. Another sect had no strength to confront the kings, nor to remain among them calling them to the religion of God the Glorified and the religion of Jesus, so they wandered through the lands and became ascetics. They are the ones of whom God the Glorified said: *'And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them.'*"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in me, confirms me, and follows me, has observed it with its proper observance. Whoever does not believe in me, those are the ones who will perish." [225] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/260.]]

Al-Dahhak and 'Atiyya narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God the Glorified prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muhammad (ﷺ). When the people of faith were reduced and only a few remained, the polytheists multiplied, the messengers passed away, and they were overpowered, they withdrew into the caves. This situation continued until a group of them disbelieved, abandoned the command and religion of God, and adopted innovation, Christianity, and Judaism, and did not observe it with its proper observance. A group remained steadfast upon the religion of Jesus until the clear proofs came to them, and God the Glorified sent Muhammad (ﷺ) while they were in that state. This is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: *"O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger..."* up to His saying: *"And God is Forgiving and Merciful."*

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Ali ibn Harb told us, saying:

Ibn Fudayl told us, saying: 'Ata' told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas.

And I was told from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Abu 'Ammar al-Husayn ibn Huraith told us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The kings after Jesus (peace be upon him) altered the Torah and the Gospel. Among them were believers who recited the Torah and the Gospel, called them to the religion of God, and commanded them to fear God the Glorified. It was said to their king: "If you gather those who have troubled you and harmed you, and then kill them, they might acknowledge what we acknowledge and enter what we are in." So their king summoned them, gathered them, and offered them the choice of death or abandoning the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel, except what they had altered in them. They said: "What do you want from us? We will take care of ourselves for you." A group of them said: "Build us a column, then raise us up to it, and give us something by which we can lift our food and drink, and we will not return to you." Another group said: "Let us travel the earth, wander, and flee as the wild beasts flee. If you overpower us in some land, then kill us." Another group said: "Build us houses in the desert, and we will dig wells and cultivate herbs, and we will not return to you or pass by you." None of them was without a close relative among them, so they did this with them. Those ones followed the path of Jesus. Then there came after them a people who had altered the Book, and a man would say: "We will be in the place of so-and-so, and worship as so-and-so worshipped, and travel as so-and-so traveled, and take houses as so-and-so took," while they were in their polytheism, with no knowledge of the faith of those whom they imitated. This is His saying, the Glorified: *"And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the pleasure of God."* He said: These righteous people innovated it. *"But they did not observe it with its proper observance"*, meaning the latter ones who came after them. *"So We gave those of them who believed their reward"*, meaning those who innovated it. *"And many of them are defiant transgressors"*: those who came after them.

He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his hermitage, the wanderer came from his wandering, and the monk from his monastery, and they believed in him and confirmed him. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, said: *"O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him), He will give you a double portion of His mercy."* He said: "Two rewards: for their faith in Jesus and the Gospel, and their faith in Muhammad and the Qur'an. *"And He will make for you a light by which you will walk,"* meaning the Qur'an. *"So that the People of the Book, who imitate them, may know that they have no power over anything of God's bounty,"* to the end of it.

Some people said: The speech ends at His saying: *"and mercy,"* then He said: *"And monasticism which they innovated, We did not prescribe it for them,"* because they abandoned the truth, ate pork, drank wine, did not perform ablution or ritual bathing from impurity, and abandoned circumcision. *"But they did not observe it with its proper observance"*, meaning the obedience and the religion; the pronoun refers to something not mentioned. *"So We gave those of them who believed their reward"*, and they are the people of compassion and mercy. *"And many of them are defiant transgressors"*, and they are the people of monasticism and innovation. Mujahid also held this view.

The meaning of His saying, *"except seeking the pleasure of God"*: "We did not command them except that, and We did not command them except to practice asceticism." Or its meaning may be: *"except seeking the pleasure of God"* according to their own claim and in their own view. And God knows best.

*"O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him), He will give you a double portion (kifl) of His mercy"*:

Two shares, for your faith in the first and your faith in the last.

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: *kiflayn* means "double," in the language of Abyssinia.

Ibn Jubayr said: Its origin is what a rider is secured with, of garments and goods, which holds him and protects him from falling. He says: this *kifl* protects you from punishment as the rider's *kifl* protects him from falling. From it comes *kafala* (guarantee), because it secures the right.

*"And He will make for you a light by which you will walk,"* among people, and on the Path, is best.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The light is the Qur'an.

Mujahid said: Guidance and clarification. *"And He will forgive you, and God is Forgiving and Merciful."*

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ja'far (may God be pleased with him) with seventy riders to al-Najashi to invite him. He arrived, invited him, and he responded and believed in him. When he was about to depart, some people among those of his kingdom who had believed in him, forty men, said: "Permit us to go to this Prophet (ﷺ), to be with him, and to row with these people across the sea, for we know the sea better than they do." They came with Ja'far to the Prophet (ﷺ), who was preparing for the battle of Uhud. When they saw the poverty and hardship in which the Muslims lived, they asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) for permission, saying: "O Messenger of God, we have wealth, and we see the hardship the Muslims are in. If you permit us, we will go back, bring our wealth, and share it with the Muslims." He permitted them, and they returned and brought their wealth and shared it with the Muslims. Then God the Glorified revealed concerning them: *"Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it..."* up to *"and from what We have provided them, they spend."* [[Surah al-Qasas: 54.]] That spending was what they shared with the Muslims. When the People of the Book who had not believed heard His saying: *"They will be given their reward twice"* [[Surah al-Qasas: 54.]], they attacked the Muslims and said: "O community of Muslims, as for whoever among us believes in your Book and ours, he has his reward twice, and whoever does not believe in your Book has a reward like your rewards. So what is your superiority over us?" Then God the Glorified revealed: *"O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger, He will give you a double portion of His mercy."* So He gave them two rewards and added light and forgiveness.

Then He said: *"So that the People of the Book may know,"* and Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited it thus: *"that they have no power..."*, the verse.

Hanan narrated from al-Kalbi, who said: They were twenty-four men who came from Yemen to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca. They were neither Jews nor Christians, but were upon the religion of the prophets, and they embraced Islam. Abu Jahl said to them: "Evil people are you, and evil is the delegation you bring to your people." They replied to him: *"And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth?"* So God the Glorified gave them and the believers among the People of the Book, 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, two rewards. They began to boast over the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "We are better than you; we have two rewards and you have one." So God the Glorified revealed: *"So that the People of the Book may know"*, the verse.

Abu 'Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sufyan told us, from Salih, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has a slave-girl, teaches her well, disciplines her well, frees her, and marries her, has two rewards. And a slave who fulfills God's right and his masters' right. And a man of the People of the Book who believed in what Moses brought, or what Jesus brought, and what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, has two rewards." [226] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/395.]]

Qatada said: The People of the Book envied the Muslims, so God the Glorified revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: The Jews said: "Soon there will come forth from us a prophet who will cut off hands and feet." When he came forth from the Arabs, they disbelieved. So God the Glorified revealed: *"So that the People of the Book may know"*, meaning that "may know" with *lā* being extra, *"that they have no power,"* meaning that they have no power, like His saying: *"that it would not return to them a word"* [[Surah Ta-Ha: 89.]]. Al-Farra' recited:

*Indeed I have guaranteed you what secures you, if you escape to the morning,*
*And are safe from the disgrace of madness, from the morning to the evening.*
*If you should descend upon the land of my people, they graze upon the acacia.*

meaning: indeed you would descend.

*"...upon anything of God's bounty"*, the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Kharja told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Sakan al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Abu Zayd al-Nahwi told us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God the Mighty and Majestic divided the reward and divided the work. It was said to the Jews: 'Work,' and they worked until midday, and it was said: 'For you is half a qirat.' It was said to the Christians: 'Work,' and they worked from midday to the afternoon prayer, and it was said: 'For you is a qirat.' It was said to the Muslims: 'Work,' and they worked from the afternoon prayer until sunset, and it was said: 'For you are two qirats.' The Jews and Christians objected to this, so God the Glorified revealed: *'So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of God's bounty, and that the bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of mighty bounty.'*" [227] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/179.]]

Abu Jahl said to them: "Evil people are you, and evil is the delegation you bring to your people." They replied to him: *"And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth?"* So God the Glorified gave them and the believers among the People of the Book, 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, two rewards. They began to boast over the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "We are better than you; we have two rewards and you have one." So God the Glorified revealed: *"So that the People of the Book may know"*, the verse.

Abu 'Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sufyan told us, from Salih, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has a slave-girl, teaches her well, disciplines her well, frees her, and marries her, has two rewards. And a slave who fulfills God's right and his masters' right. And a man of the People of the Book who believed in what Moses brought, or what Jesus brought, and what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, has two rewards." [226] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/395.]]

Qatada said: The People of the Book envied the Muslims, so God the Glorified revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: The Jews said: "Soon there will come forth from us a prophet who will cut off hands and feet." When he came forth from the Arabs, they disbelieved. So God the Glorified revealed: *"So that the People of the Book may know"*, meaning that "may know" with *lā* being extra, *"that they have no power,"* meaning that they have no power, like His saying: *"that it would not return to them a word"* [[Surah Ta-Ha: 89.]]. Al-Farra' recited:

*Indeed I have guaranteed you what secures you, if you escape to the morning,*
*And are safe from the disgrace of madness, from the morning to the evening.*
*If you should descend upon the land of my people, they graze upon the acacia.*

meaning: indeed you would descend.

*"...upon anything of God's bounty"*, the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Kharja told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Sakan al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Abu Zayd al-Nahwi told us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God the Mighty and Majestic divided the reward and divided the work. It was said to the Jews: 'Work,' and they worked until midday, and it was said: 'For you is half a qirat.' It was said to the Christians: 'Work,' and they worked from midday to the afternoon prayer, and it was said: 'For you is a qirat.' It was said to the Muslims: 'Work,' and they worked from the afternoon prayer until sunset, and it was said: 'For you are two qirats.' The Jews and Christians objected to this, so God the Glorified revealed: *'So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of God's bounty, and that the bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of mighty bounty.'*" [227] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/179.]]
